categories.main_business_segments: Hansol Chemical operates primarily in three segments: precision chemicals including hydrogen peroxide, benzoyl peroxide, and sodium dithionite; paper and environmental products such as latex and polymer flocculants; and electronic and secondary battery materials including semiconductor precursors, display resins, quantum dots, and lithium-ion battery materials. Its major subsidiary, Tapex, focuses on electronic materials like tapes for secondary batteries, displays, semiconductors, and consumer packaging films.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company utilizes advanced chemical synthesis and polymerization technologies for precision chemicals and paper/environmental products. For electronic and battery materials, it develops and manufactures semiconductor precursors, display resins, and battery binders using proprietary chemical processes. Continuous R&D efforts focus on new grades, quality improvement, and commercialization of cutting-edge materials such as silicon anodes and quantum dots.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers include semiconductor manufacturers (Samsung Electronics, SK Hynix, TSMC), display companies (Samsung Display), battery producers (Samsung SDI, LG Energy Solution, SK On), paper and textile industries, and environmental treatment sectors. Tapex serves electronics and consumer goods companies including Samsung Display, LG Energy Solution, Murata, Emart, and Starbucks. The markets span semiconductor, display, battery, paper, textile, and environmental industries.
categories.geographic_coverage: Hansol Chemical operates mainly in South Korea with production facilities in Ulsan and Jeonju, and exports to Asia (including Taiwan, China, Japan), the Middle East, and global semiconductor hubs such as the US. Tapex has subsidiaries in Malaysia and China and serves global customers. The company is expanding manufacturing capacity in domestic industrial complexes and targeting international markets.
categories.supply_chain_position: Hansol Chemical functions primarily as a midstream chemical manufacturer supplying essential raw and intermediate materials to downstream industries such as semiconductor, display, battery, paper, and environmental sectors. Tapex operates downstream by producing specialized tapes and films used in electronic device assembly and packaging. The company is positioned as a key supplier within the chemical and electronic materials supply chains.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: The company prioritizes R&D in new business areas related to semiconductors, displays, and secondary batteries, focusing on developing new grades and improving quality of existing products like hydrogen peroxide and latex. It invests in advanced materials such as semiconductor precursors, quantum dots, and silicon anode materials for batteries. R&D expenditure has increased steadily, supporting commercialization of innovative products and customer co-development initiatives.
categories.revenue_model: Hansol Chemical generates revenue primarily through product sales of chemicals, electronic materials, and battery components. Sales channels include direct sales to affiliated and non-affiliated companies and indirect sales via distributors. The company also earns revenue from product exports and provides some technical services. Tapex's revenue is mainly from sales of electronic tapes and consumer packaging products.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: Hansol Chemical holds leading market shares in key products such as latex (43%), sodium dithionite (65%), and benzoyl peroxide (72%) in Korea, competing with companies like Kumho Petrochemical, Trinseo, and LG Chem. The company is recognized for stable supply and quality in precision chemicals and is expanding its presence in electronic and battery materials. Tapex competes in electronic materials and consumer packaging with a focus on innovation and market share expansion.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2023, Hansol Chemical reported consolidated sales of approximately 771.7 billion KRW, a 12.9% decrease from the previous year, with operating profit of 124.1 billion KRW. Total assets stood at about 1.35 trillion KRW with a healthy debt ratio of 43.5%. Tapex contributed sales of 143.6 billion KRW in 2023. The company has shown a declining sales trend recently but maintains strong financial stability and continues investing in growth areas.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: Hansol Chemical emphasizes high-quality, customized chemical products and advanced electronic materials that meet stringent customer requirements in semiconductor, display, and battery industries. Its competitive edge lies in stable supply, proprietary technologies, diversified product portfolio, and active R&D collaboration with customers. Tapex differentiates through innovative tape solutions tailored for electronics and consumer packaging, supporting customers’ performance and sustainability goals.
